chapter: Chapter 2: The Yoga of Knowledge (Sankhya Yoga)
text: The contacts of the senses with external objects, O son of Kunti, give rise to cold and heat, pleasure and pain. They are fleeting and impermanent; endure them with equanimity, O descendant of Bharata.

chapter: Chapter 2: The Yoga of Knowledge (Sankhya Yoga)
text: The soul is never born nor does it die; having once been, it never ceases to be. Unborn, eternal, changeless, and primeval, it is not slain when the body is slain.

chapter: Chapter 2: The Yoga of Knowledge (Sankhya Yoga)
text: Thy right is to the work alone, never to its fruits; let not the fruits of action be thy motive, nor let thy attachment be to inaction.

chapter: Chapter 2: The Yoga of Knowledge (Sankhya Yoga)
text: He whose mind is untroubled in the midst of sorrows, who is indifferent amid pleasures, and who is free from passion, fear, and anger, is called a sage of steadfast wisdom.

chapter: Chapter 2: The Yoga of Knowledge (Sankhya Yoga)
text: Brooding on objects of sense begets attraction; from attraction grows desire; from desire comes anger. From anger arises delusion; from delusion confusion of memory; from confusion of memory the ruin of reason; and from ruin of reason a man perishes.

chapter: Chapter 3: The Yoga of Action (Karma Yoga)
text: Therefore, constantly perform the action which ought to be done, without attachment; for by performing action without attachment, man reaches the Supreme.

chapter: Chapter 3: The Yoga of Action (Karma Yoga)
text: Whatsoever a great man does, that very thing other men do; whatever standard he sets up, the world follows.

chapter: Chapter 3: The Yoga of Action (Karma Yoga)
text: Better is one's own duty, though devoid of merit, than the duty of another well performed. Better is death in the discharge of one's own duty; the duty of another is fraught with peril.

chapter: Chapter 4: The Yoga of Wisdom (Jnana Yoga)
text: Truly there is no purifier in this world like wisdom. He who is perfected in yoga finds it in his own Self in due season.

chapter: Chapter 4: The Yoga of Wisdom (Jnana Yoga)
text: The man of faith, who is devoted and has restrained his senses, attains knowledge; and having attained knowledge, he swiftly attains supreme peace.

chapter: Chapter 6: The Yoga of Self-Control (Dhyana Yoga)
text: Let a man lift himself by his own Self, let him not debase himself; for the Self alone is the friend of the self, and the Self alone is the enemy of the self.

chapter: Chapter 6: The Yoga of Self-Control (Dhyana Yoga)
text: From whatever cause the restless and unsteady mind wanders away, let him restrain it and bring it back under the control of the Self alone.

chapter: Chapter 16: The Divine and Demonic Natures
text: Fearlessness, purity of heart, steadfastness in knowledge, charity, self-control, sacrifice, study of scriptures, austerity, uprightness, non-violence, truth, freedom from anger, renunciation, tranquility, and compassion to all living beings—these are the endowments of him who is born with the divine nature.

chapter: Chapter 16: The Divine and Demonic Natures
text: Triple is the gate of hell, destructive of the self: lust, anger, and greed. Therefore, let a man abandon these three.
